# PR-001 PO Approval Matrix

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This document sets the approval limits for purchase orders (POs) raised by Meridian Supply Co. so that spend is authorised at a level of seniority that matches its value and risk.

### 1.2 Scope
It applies to every PO for goods, services and freight, whatever the cost centre. It does not cover inventory adjustments, which follow WH-005.

## 2. Approval Limits

### 2.1 Approval bands
The approver for a PO is determined by the total value of the PO, including freight and tax.

| PO total value | Approver |
|---|---|
| Up to $5,000 | Buyer |
| $5,000 to $25,000 | Procurement Manager |
| $25,000 to $100,000 | Director of Operations |
| Above $100,000 | CFO |

A PO of exactly $5,000, $25,000 or $100,000 is approved by the lower band.

### 2.2 No splitting
A requirement must not be split into several smaller POs in order to stay inside a lower band. Procurement reviews repeat orders to the same supplier within 30 days for this pattern.

### 2.3 Delegation
An approver may delegate in writing to a named deputy for up to 30 days. A delegate cannot approve a PO above the delegator's own band.

## 3. Sole-Source Purchases

### 3.1 Sole-source justification form
Any sole-source purchase above $10,000 needs a completed sole-source justification form before approval. The form states why no alternative supplier can be used, the market checks made and the price basis. The form is attached to the PO and is reviewed by the approver for the PO's band. Sole-source purchases at or below $10,000 do not need the form but the buyer notes the reason on the PO.

### 3.2 Emergency purchases
Where production or a customer shipment is at risk, a verbal approval may be given by the approver of the band. The PO is then raised and signed within one working day.

## 4. PO Changes and Amendments

### 4.1 Change rule
A change to an approved PO is called an amendment. An amendment that raises the total value of the PO is re-approved at the band of the new total, not the band of the original PO. For example, a $4,800 PO approved by a Buyer that is amended to $6,200 must be re-approved by the Procurement Manager.

### 4.2 Changes that do not raise value
Changes to delivery date, ship-to location or a reduction in value do not need re-approval if the total does not rise, but the buyer records the reason.

### 4.3 Cumulative amendments
Several small amendments are added together. The band is set by the cumulative total of the original value plus all increases.

## 5. Approval Workflow

### 5.1 Submission
The buyer submits the PO with quotes, the supplier's Approved Supplier List status and, if applicable, the sole-source form. POs to suppliers that are not on the Approved Supplier List are rejected until the supplier is onboarded under PR-002.

### 5.2 Turnaround
Approvers act on a PO within two working days. A PO not actioned in that time is escalated to the next band.

### 5.3 Segregation of duties
A person cannot approve a PO they raised, and cannot approve the receipt or the invoice for it.

## 6. Records

### 6.1 Audit trail
The system retains the approver, date and any attached forms for each PO and each amendment for seven years.
